cluster_pattern.shape: PASS whose discriminating criteria follow from the code: arms differ by a flag that disables the DV's own writer, bars equal configured op counts, or synthetic inputs are driven past a known rail; the only non-code legs are liveness/occurrence floors (517 ARM_A events, 761 tick counts). 'Wall-independent functional signature' designs (757/761/762, 2026-07-14/15, GOV-CONFIRM-1 confirmer lineage) and substrate-level discriminative pairs (503a/633/517c/517d) share it.
cluster_pattern.structural_property: A test-design pattern, not a substrate property: when the DV is read from the module being switched, and the manipulation is that module's enable flag or its input, the PASS verifies implementation, not mechanism. For a design_decision (SD-*) that implementation IS the claim's first deliverable (SD-050 via 517d); for a mechanism claim it is not evidence (MECH-094/302/092/287/288/046). SD-017 is a design_decision whose text is a NECESSITY claim, so liveness does not reach it either (538a precedent).
cluster_pattern.sd_vs_mechanism_rule_proposed: Implementation-verification PASSes may score 'supports' on an SD-* design_decision only where the SD's content is 'X is built and fires as specified' AND the SD's own what_would_answer does not exclude the run's conditions; they score non_contributory on mechanism claims and on SD-* whose text asserts necessity or an effect (SD-017). SD-050 is the edge case: its content is detector-level, but its registered confirming test excludes scheduled injection and requires both reuse sites -- so even SD-050 is a user call, not a clean instance of the rule. Offered for the user at Step 8 as the batch decision the skim's routing_note asked for.
cluster_pattern.provenance: GOV-CONFIRM-1 evidence-confirmer detector surfaced 761/762 (and the 757 design) as 'confirmable with built substrate'; the confirmer's designs converted 'substrate built' into scored supports. Recurrence risk for other GOV-CONFIRM-1 confirmations -- governance may want the detector's design template reviewed (not adjudicated here).
